description: The image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each illustrating the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—as they relate to performance or outcomes in a Zero-Shot setting, likely from the paper “Knowledge Crosswords: Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language Models.” The charts use a consistent color legend: teal for N+K+, yellow for N−K+, orange for N−K−, and red for N+K−. In the “easy” chart, N+K+ dominates at 55.4%, followed by N−K+ at 38.3%, N−K− at 4.6%, and N+K− at 1.7%. The “medium” chart shows a similar trend with N+K+ at 58.8%, N−K+ at 35.4%, N−K− at 4.0%, and N+K− at 1.8%. In the “hard” chart, the distribution becomes more balanced: N−K− and N−K+ each occupy 37.9% and 37.3% respectively, while N+K+ drops to 18.1% and N+K− remains low at 6.7%. All slices are labeled with their exact percentages, and the charts are visually grouped under the “Zero-Shot” label, suggesting a comparative analysis of model behavior across difficulty levels.
